From voltages and currents measured at the PCC, a feature extraction stage was employed, where root mean square, crest factor, form factor and total harmonic distortion were calculated. These features were used as inputs to decision trees responsible to identify the contribution side (none, utility-side, consumer-side or both sides). Next, adaptive neural-fuzzy inference systems were used to estimate the harmonic contribution, if necessary, for each side. The decision trees were able to reach more than 99% of accuracy, while the neural-fuzzy systems obtained mean square errors between 1.1e-2 and 3.0e-9.

articleTitle: The Empirical Effect of Fleet Optimization on Synchronization and Rebound Effects in Heat Pump Water Heaters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Demand response is a growing concept in light of the internet of things and an increasing need for grid flexibility. Water heaters are one of the preferred devices for providing demand response for grid services and peak management due to their capability to store energy. The efficient use of water heaters for demand response requires consideration of the associated load effects such as synchronization of device schedules and rebound effect. These effects present a significant challenge. Despite the importance of the mentioned effects for water heater queuing and scheduling, there has been no effort to quantify and empirically validate their impact. This study attempts to address this gap by offering two methods - Ward clustering and Euclidean K-means - to evaluate the extent of synchronization in a fleet of 42 water heaters in Atlanta, GA. Using the aforementioned methods on the measured data, we find evidence of convergence of water heater loads as a result of optimization compared to an idle period and analyzed their impact.

articleTitle: Identification of Atypical Billings of Consumer Units by Artificial Intelligence Techniques to Reduce Non-Technical Losses in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The article presents the development of a computational platform to identify atypical billings in low voltage consumer units using the Isolation Forest algorithm, aiming to detect peculiar changes in energy consumption and/or evidence of fraud. The algorithm analyzes a large set of historical data (up to 10 years) and identifies “atypical” monthly billings among consumer units with the same type of load, generating a list of candidate units for subsequent inspection in the field. Preliminary tests carried out at a medium-sized distribution concessionaire showed an assertiveness rate of 91.70%, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for the large-scale identification of anomalies in the monthly billing data of consumer units.

Author Keywords: Detection and Identification of Electrical Losses

articleTitle: A Comparison Between Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization for Economic Dispatch in a Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Microgrids (MGs) and distributed energy resources (DERs) have gained popularity as a path to develop a more resilient, sustainable, and efficient energy infrastructure. Although photovoltaic (PV) systems and wind generators are common technologies in MGs, their variability and uncertainty pose reliability challenges. Battery energy storage systems (BESS) are integrated as backup solutions to address these issues. Energy management (EM) can perform economic dispatch (ED), which involves determining the most cost-effective combination of energy generation sources. In this paper, genetic algorithms (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) were used to optimize the use of BESS in an MG, considering discharge cost factors that affect BESS lifetime. The results obtained reveal that both algorithms efficiently performed ED, however, PSO exhibited superior cost efficiency in its optimization outcomes and outpaced GA by 37.5% in terms of speed. Consequently, PSO showcased improved precision and swiftness when compared to GA in this task.

articleTitle: Modeling of Inverter-Based Resources for Protection Studies Considering Momentary Cessation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper addresses the impact of the momentary cessation of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) on the protection of distribution systems. Momentary cessation is one of the require-ments in IEEE 1547 standard that requires IBRs to momentarily cease the energization when a severe disturbance (e.g., fault) occurs and large deviations in the system voltage or frequency are observed. This will enable IBRs to also accommodate the voltage-ride-through requirements since they can be energized again if the fault is cleared before the ride-through time. The momentary cessation modeling in PSS®CAPE and Matlab/Simulink is elab-orated. The paper highlights the impact of momentary cessation on the fault current and operation of time over current elements by simulating a modified version of the IEEE 123 node system in PSS®CAPE.

articleTitle: Cooperative Microgrids: Technical Feasibility of the PREB's Microgrid Rule
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: In 2018, after hurricane Maria, the Puerto Rico Energy Bureau published a new standard to regulate the implementation of microgrids in Puerto Rico (PREB Microgrid Rule). In this paper, different scenarios were developed to study the feasibility of microgrids that satisfy the rules set forth by the standard. The models used to represent the microgrid and the complete electrical system were implemented in MATLAB/Simulink. Utilizing OPAL-RT, a robust simulation hardware, the present study conducted a series of test cases to emulate the behavior of these microgrids while meeting the requirements specified by the PREB microgrid rule.

articleTitle: Impact of Single-Phase PV Systems on the Harmonic Distortions of Costa Rican LV Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation in low voltage (LV) distribution networks may not only impact the power quality of the grid in terms of overvoltages, but it also can bring about interactions with the harmonic distortions in the grid. However, large-scale harmonic impact studies pose technical difficulties when working with inverter-based resources (IBR) such as the complex models required for simulation, computational burden, and the uncertainty of vendor-specific control parameters and topology. This paper presents a sensitivity analysis of a real LV distribution circuit model in Costa Rica, changing the topology and parameters of single-phase (1ph) PV generators to show their impact on the harmonic distortion levels. This study was commissioned by Costa Rican distribution utilities to evaluate if PVs are to blame for the harmonic pollution of modern LV grids. Overall, the results show that the PVs lower the grid distortion levels. It was also determined that the measurement filter cutoff frequency, the front-end filter size, and the feedforward topology are the most relevant parameters in these studies.

articleTitle: Insights of Residential Smart Meter Data in Australia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The use of smart meters is increasing worldwide, offering valuable data for distribution companies. It can be used to run analytics or carry out simulations that can improve different planning and operational activities. However, before using real smart meter data, it is important to understand its nature and characteristics. This paper provides insights from real smart meter data that can help distribution engineers and researchers define the most suitable ways of using such data. The investigated smart meter data corresponds to three distribution companies in Victoria, Australia, and includes voltage magnitudes and currents (magnitude, sign, and power factor, or real and imaginary values) recorded every 5 minutes over periods of approximately 12 months between 2020 and 2021. The analysis shows the relationships between active and reactive power, and voltages, highlighting the net capacitive household behaviour, different PV export limits, and Volt-var responses of PV inverters.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo-Based Approach for Obtaining the Marginal Costs of Grid Reinforcement for the Accommodation of Rooftop PVs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Worldwide, the installed capacity of rooftop photovoltaic systems (PVs) has been increasing rapidly, faster than the traditional load increase rate. Differently from the loads, the simultaneity factor of rooftop PV generation is roughly 1.0, resulting in higher violations of technical and regulatory limits. One of the most widely adopted solutions to accommodate rooftop PVs is to perform grid reinforcements, such as reconductoring and circuit sectionalization. In several countries, the investments in grid reinforcement are transferred to the customers as energy tariff, impacting the economy. Because of that, the Brazilian Electricity Regulatory Agency (ANEEL) is dedicating efforts to estimating the benefits and costs of integrating distributed generators into the power systems. In this context, this paper presents a Monte Carlo-based methodology that obtains the marginal costs of grid reinforcement for a Brazilian distribution utility, i.e., how much the installation of 1 kWp of rooftop PV costs. It is shown that the order the PVs are installed strongly affects the marginal cost and that a small part of the circuits is responsible for most reinforcement costs. Utilities and regulatory agencies can adopt this method to perform similar estimations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different BESS Dispatch Strategies to Improve Low-Voltage Distribution Grid Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The dissemination of small distributed generation systems by photovoltaic source (DGPV) has caused daytime overvoltages in low-voltage distribution systems. Battery energy storage systems (BESS), when operating in parallel with DGPV, may not only expand the energy benefits brought about by these systems but also mitigate the undesired effects associated with the operation of such intermittent energy sources. The incorporation of BESS on low-voltage networks can solve not only the problems of overvoltage produced through DGPV operation but also the undervoltage observed in periods of greater demand on the system, which normally occur at the beginning of the evening, when the DGPVs are inoperative. Another benefit arising from the incorporation of BESS is the reduction in the loading of distribution transformers, increasing the available capacity of such systems. This work presents an analysis of the different approaches for dispatching BESS, while aiming at improving the performance of low-voltage distribution grids.

articleTitle: Smart Data Mapping for Connecting Power System Model and Geospatial Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Knowing the geospatial locations of power system model elements and linking load models with end users and their communities are the foundation for analyzing system resilience and vulnerability to natural hazards. However, power system models and geospatial data for power grid assets are often developed asynchronously without close coordination. Creating a direct mapping between the two is a challenging task, mainly due to heterogeneous data structures, target uses, historical legacies, and human errors. This work aims to build an automatic data mapping workflow to connect the two, and to support energy grid resilience studies for Puerto Rico. The primary steps in this workflow include constructing graphs using geospatial data, and aligning them to the transmission networks defined in the power system data. The results have been evaluated against existing manual mapping practices for part of the Puerto Rico Power Grid model to illustrate the performance of such auto-mapping solutions.

articleTitle: Integration and Assessment of Photovoltaic Systems in Puerto Rican Communities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper presents an study of the integration of photovoltaic systems in Puerto Rican communities focused on the analysis of the hosting capacity of the power system and the limits regulation around the voltage profiles, thermal limits for transformers, and community benefits. For the study, two communities in Puerto Rico was considered, and a brief description of load consumption and power system characteristics are presented. For development of this research work, an open distributed system simulator was used with Matlab as Component Object Model interface. The obtained results allow to analyze the effects of photovoltaic integration in the power grid, as well as the benefits of the renewable resources installation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Integrated-Energy Projects: A Simplified Tool for Non-Expert Project Developers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Renewable-energy (RE) resources have become economically feasible options to cover local energy-needs. This fact has motivated many small entrepreneurs to start businesses related to RE. Yet, these new non-expert project developers usually offer either electrical or thermal solutions. However, the integration of both could result into an even more cost-effective solution. Although tools to design optimal solutions exist, these are typically too difficult or unreachable (due to cost or language) for small developers. In this paper, we present a simplified tool, targeted for non-expert developers, to compare electrical and thermal needs with energy potential. The paper is not intended to show new ways to evaluate energy projects, but rather to help small-scale RE developers to implement integrated-energy projects. We show the application of the tool into a project in Chile. The results show the daily-annual variation of the electrical and thermal demands, and local energy-resources in the same format.

articleTitle: Electromobility Pattern Modeling for Estimating the Charging Infrastructure of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The growth in the Electric Vehicle (EV) fleet increases the need for new Public Charging Stations (PCS). However, the conflicting interests of stakeholders make charging infrastructure planning highly complex. In practice, the chosen locations are as accessible as possible, predominantly in more central regions of cities. Above all, providing appropriate locations is essential since the recharge demand can impact the power distribution grid in technical, operational, and planning aspects. Given the above, this work proposes a methodology for estimating suitable locations for installing PCS. An approach based on transport modeling is carried out to evaluate electromobility patterns considering the routes with high EV traffic areas and their state of charge. The infrastructure is determined from the location-allocation problem, and the proposal is tested in a large metropolis considering two EV penetration scenarios.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of Low Power Factor Penalties Due to Photovoltaic Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper presents a techno-economic analysis of low power factor penalties for prosumers and distribution companies. Prosumers are consumers who install distributed generators, typically photovoltaic systems. Penalties related to low power factor infractions at the point of common coupling may be imposed on this category of consumers, which they had not encountered in their energy bills prior to the installation of the photovoltaic system. Additionally, distribution companies can face penalties if there is a reduction in the power factor of high and medium voltage substations. In the paper, an optimization model is employed to determine the power factor adjustment of photovoltaic inverters used by prosumers. This adjustment can mitigate power factor violations at the point of common coupling without the need for reactive power compensation devices. As a case study, an urban distribution feeder of a metropolitan region in Sao Paulo, Brazil is selected, considering five photovoltaic generation scenarios for a typical day of operation and a 30% penetration of photovoltaic systems in the electric grid. The findings suggest that distribution companies should devise strategies to incentivize prosumers to improve their power factor.

articleTitle: Reliability and Unavailability Within the Operational Planning of Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This article introduces a methodology that contributes to the integrated planification of distribution systems by covering reliability and unavailability within the operational decisions that are planned and executed by the Energy Distribution Companies. A computational application is developed in Python software, with the aim of automatizing and optimizing response times. The decision to perform maintenance activities on electrical feeders is dynamic and requires efficiency, effectiveness and quick response. The methodology was applied in the distribution system of Quito Electric Company - EEQ in Ecuador. The results reveal a contribution to decisions within maintenance and operation. EEQ is currently one of the top three companies with the best service quality indicators, according to the ranking established by the Ministry of Energy and Non-Renewable Natural Resources of Ecuador.

Author Keywords: integrated planning of distributed energy resources
maintenance and operation of distribution systems

articleTitle: Comparison of Battery Degradation in a Microgrid Operating Under Two Different DER Scheduling Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This document provides a comparison of the degradation for a Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery used into a PV based grid-connected microgrid with two scheduling cases, the first one with a rule-based battery scheduling and the second one with an optimization based on a Mixed Integer Linear Problem (MILP) strategy. For the last case, the objective function consists of minimizing the energy cost for a house with a photovoltaic system in Puerto Rico. Both methods have been evaluated within one month window and one hour step in order to obtain the battery’ state of charge (SoC). With this information, the battery degradation was calculated based on Rainflow - Counting (RFC) algorithm to obtain the cheapest and least aging battery degradation, obtained from the results, a direct relationship between the SoC at the final of the day and the battery degradation.

articleTitle: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Method for Fast Voltage Regulation using Distributed Wind Turbine Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper proposes a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) voltage regulation method for distribution systems with presence of Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs). The control employs reactive power injection or absorption in three WTGs to regulate feeder voltages. A weighted global voltage metric is calculated to summarize nodes' voltages according to their relevance. Three independent RL Agents are trained using policy parameter sharing. Models are trained and tested on real-time Hardware-In-the-Loop setup. The proposed control effectively regulates voltage through the system, bringing median and mean voltages closer to 1 p.u. and reducing standard deviation.

articleTitle: Ground Fault Overvoltage Analysis of Submarine-Fed IBR-Dominated Networked Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Nowadays research in the areas of power system resilience and renewable energy resources have been progressing at unprecedented pace. This reflects the current focus of Energy Justice and creates an environment suitable for augmenting electricity service to vulnerable communities. One the one hand, resilience strategies often result in reinforcing or rebuilding portions of a power system network, whereas on the other this represents an opportunity to develop a system to become ready to house larger amounts of renewable energy and by extension microgrids, which can further increase resiliency. This is particularly important in grid-edge systems that are highly dependent on supplies that lack redundancy. This paper addresses the legacy issue of effective grounding, as a grid edge supply is improved in a system where the system operator is building two networked microgrids in two small islands supplied by submarine cables. This is the first system-of-systems of its kind and the farthest from a main grid where the only interconnection is through such vulnerable supply, which by way of construction inherently is ineffectively grounded, making the system prone to temporary overvoltages. In this work, the author analyzes the problem by providing an analytical overview of temporary overvoltage management. The paper proposes mitigating these interconnection issues by using neutral grounding elements connected to coupling transformers and analyzing requirements for inverter negative-sequence current injection to ground faults.

articleTitle: Centralized Secondary Microgrid Controller Based on Smith Predictor and Fuzzy Logic to Address Communication Delay Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel solution for addressing delay issues in islanded microgrids through a centralized secondary control based on the Smith predictor, enhanced with an intelligence fuzzy logic block. The fuzzy logic block serves as an artificial intelligence tool that, estimate the delay in the system and feeds it to the Smith predictor. This innovative approach allows the controller to effectively handle both fixed and variable delays, thereby improving the overall stability and dynamic response of the microgrid. By adapting its parameters based on the estimated delay, the controller ensures the reliable operation of the microgrid, enabling a rapid restoration of frequency and voltage for optimal power sharing. Different case studies are conducted to validate the significant enhancements achieved through the integration of the proposed intelligence control system.

articleTitle: Hybrid Portable Power Station with Several Sources of Energy for Emergencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: After the devastation caused by recent extreme events that impact Puerto Rico (PR), there has been a strong adoption of renewable energy sources (RES) due to the persistent power outages. In this paper, the design, built, and testing of a hybrid portable power station to supply power of residential critical loads is presented. The system consists of three sources of renewable generation (solar, wind, and mechanical bike) and batteries for storage purpose. The proposed system was designed to supply approximately 6KWh/day with 24 hours of autonomy. Results demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed system, particularly in isolated communities of PR.

articleTitle: Characterization of Hurricane Boundary Layer Winds on Power Towers Using a High-Resolution LES Weather Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: During hurricanes, power transmission and distribution systems are highly susceptible to structural failures due to constant exposure to strong winds. This article focuses on the impacts of Hurricane Maria (H-Maria) in Puerto Rico (PR) as an exceptional case study. The storm caused extensive damage to the power infrastructure, including transmission lines, distribution lines, and substations. The study highlights the importance of accurately representing the turbulent hurricane boundary layer (HBL) in simulations, particularly in areas with complex terrain. The research employs a Large Eddy Simulation (LES) approach within the Weather Research and Forecasting model (WRF) to recreate H-Maria's winds. The simulation demonstrates improved accuracy in representing the HBL, showcasing stronger wind velocities in mountainous areas where the power towers are situated. Further analysis reveals significant downward motion and turbulence intensity within the HBL at the location of the transmission line. These findings highlight the heightened risk of structural failure and damage due to fluctuating wind directions and the complex terrain's amplifying effect.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Networked Community Microgrid with High Solar Penetration Considering Control Dynamics of Inverter-Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Microgrids help facilitate the integration of renewable energy in distribution-level grids and increase the resilience of the electric grid to extreme weather, especially in rural areas. Compared to traditional microgrids, a networked microgrid leverages multiple grid-forming sources to form a potential meshed grid and is more flexible in operation. This paper demonstrates the simulation modeling of an actual networked microgrid located in Adjuntas, Puerto Rico. The model contains representations of power inverters that connect the battery energy storage systems and photovoltaic generation systems to the networked microgrid and is capable of simulating fast grid transients as well as long-term operation of the networked microgrid. The modeling technique for power inverters allows the time-efficient simulation of the microgrid with a minimal penalty on model accuracy.

articleTitle: Framework for Distribution Systems Planning Considering Probabilistic Criteria
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This work presents a computational tool to support the planning of power distribution networks (DNs) considering probabilistic criteria. The proposed computational tool is composed of four modules: (i) Prosumers; (ii) Data Processing; (iii) Feeders, Voltage, and Power Losses; and (iv) Distribution Transformers and Reliability. The developed modules help evaluate the performance of medium voltage DNs, considering the presence of distributed energy resources (DERs). Probabilistic operating scenarios are generated through the processing of measured data of distribution feeders, whereas prosumers are represented using an energy disaggregation method. We also determined operational indicators related to loading, losses, voltage, and reliability. Furthermore, critical points of DNs are identified based on the estimation of financial compensation for violating the reliability indices assessed by network zones. Finally, the proposed computational tool can be applied to compare operational and reliability indicators, whether considering a single feeder or a set of feeders.

articleTitle: New ANN-Based Method for Islanding Detection in Distribution Systems with PV Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Anti-islanding protection of distributed generators (DG) is typically performed by conventional schemes based on measurements of voltage magnitude and frequency. Nevertheless, these schemes pose challenges regarding the definition of threshold values for differentiating islanding conditions from other disturbances that may occur in distribution systems, such as voltage sag or swell. In this context, schemes based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) can be useful to identify patterns in voltage signals, making it possible to precisely differentiate islanding events from any other events. However, in general, the ANN training process is not simple, since it involves the following definitions: suitable neural network topology; data window length; sampling rate; and a representative training set for the analyzed power grid. Therefore, this paper presents a methodology for training and testing an ANN MLP-type for islanding detection of photovoltaic (PV) DG. A real scenario representing the Federal University of ABC (Brazil) was modelled, thus allowing to develop and test the proposed ANN-based solution with practical data. The results show that ANNs are an interesting alternative to perform the islanding detection of PV DG.

articleTitle: Fault-Induced Delayed Voltage Recovery Assessment in the Colombian Power System Using Synchrophasor Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The paper presents a methodology for assessing the phenomenon of fault-induced delayed voltage recovery (FIDVR) using data from phasor measurement units (PMU). The methodology allows the processing of time series of bus voltages in which indicators of voltage magnitude evolution performance are calculated and compared with technical criteria thresholds to evaluate the phenomenon, defining when, where, and with what magnitude FIDVR occurs in each analyzed time series. The methodology is validated using data from the Colombian power system operation obtained from PMUs installed in several substations that centralize information with the wide-area monitoring system (WAMS). The results show that this methodology can quantify and locate the FIDVR phenomenon in response to faults occurring in the national interconnected system using synchrophasor measurements. This methodology has been converted into the strategy of the National Dispatch Center of Colombia to monitor FIDVR and determine new reactive compensation requirements based on real data.

articleTitle: Potential Application for Oscillating Water Column Generation in Puerto Rico
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The world is being pushed to explore for new sources of power generation to fulfill the growing demand for electric power as demand grows and the cost of electricity continues to rise. Increased use of renewable energy in the energy mix has prompted significant R&D initiatives in recent decades. The island condition of Puerto Rico opens the possibility to integrate ocean energy technologies as power sources. In this work oscillating water columns (OWC) is analysed in the context of integrate these systems as part of coastal erosion mitigation projects. The scenario is the northeast coast of the island. Energy potential is considered and economic feasibility. A comparison on interconnection with a Photovoltaic (PV) power system is made to see the pertinency of the discussion of the integration of diverse renewable energy sources to the grid.

articleTitle: Meteorological Data-Driven Traffic Flow Forecasting Using Intelligent Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper proposes the incorporation of meteorological and typical seasonal Historical Traffic Flow (HTF) data into Deep Learning (DL) algorithms using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Machine Learning (ML) algorithm using Random Forest Tree (RFT) to enhance the forecasting accuracy of Electric Vehicle (EV) traffic flow through electrified transportation infrastructures. The forecasting accuracy is validated by comparing performance results of three scenarios where the first case employs only HTF, the second utilizes HTF plus typical seasonal values, and the final case considers HTF plus typical seasonal values plus meteorological data. Test results demonstrate a significant improvement in forecasting accuracy of EV traffic flow for 6-hour-ahead and 24-hour-ahead horizons.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo-Based Transmission and Subtransmission Recovery Simulation of Hurricanes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: High-impact low-probability (HILP) events can wreak havoc on electric power systems without appropriate preparedness. In this paper, the recent development of a tool, named Recovery Simulator and Analysis (RSA), is described and demonstrated. While there are many issues to consider when recovering electric power systems, the focus of RSA is on the coordination of transmission and subtransmission recovery with generation dispatch to minimize unserved energy. RSA focuses on recovery simulation to evaluate resilience as part of a planning process. RSA is demonstrated on an approximately 1400-bus Puerto Rican power system for 100 simulated instances of Hurricane Maria. Analysis of the recovery determines how many lines are critical to the recovery and which loads may experience delayed recovery. The results demonstrate the potential uses of RSA for identifying recovery decisions with low unserved energy and for identifying assets critical to recovery which can then be hardened prior to a HILP event.

articleTitle: Enhancing Reliability and Resilience via Optimal Transmission Project Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for optimizing the selection and scheduling of a portfolio of transmission projects proposed to enhance transmission system reliability and resilience. The methodology focuses on selecting and scheduling transmission projects across the various geographic zones to improve system reliability and resilience after the projects are completed while minimizing potential customer and critical load interruptions during the construction phase. The proposed optimization model aims to achieve or exceed reliability and resilience targets during the planning horizon while accommodating budgetary constraints and limitations on crew availability. A case study demonstrates the approach's effectiveness in simultaneously improving reliability metrics and resilience impact.

articleTitle: Optimal Coordinated Operation of V2G Charging Stations for Improving EV Hosting Capacity in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper proposes a mixed-integer non-linear programming model (MINLP) for the optimal coordinated operation of charging stations with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology to increase the hosting capacity of a distribution network. The analysis mechanism considers voltage violations and minimum state of charge, while the objective function searches to minimize technical losses on the entire circuit. The results of studies using one test system certify the benefits of the proposed strategy in using V2G to increase the hosting capacity of distribution networks.

articleTitle: Microgrid Design Toolkit Evaluation and Trade-offs Analysis for Rural Community in Cayey Puerto Rico
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Puerto Rico's power infrastructure was devastated by the passage of Hurricanes Irma and Maria in 2017. It highlighted the lack of resilience of the system and left the island with unreliable electric service for years after. Community leaders are looking for reliable alternatives to supply their energy needs. Three microgrid design alternatives are evaluated for a rural community in a mountainous region in Puerto Rico. The three alternatives consider centralized and decentralized options for diesel generation and energy storage in lithium-ion batteries, while having distributed roof-mounted photovoltaic generation. The trade-off space of solutions for the three alternatives is presented in the form of a Pareto frontier. Optimization results for the centralized alternative slightly favor diesel and cost seems attractive. Less aggregated alternatives favor solar generation, making it the preferred alternative, especially to take advantage of Puerto Rico's net energy metering program.

articleTitle: Power System Modeling for Hardware-In-the-Loop Testing of A Traveling-Wave-Based Relay
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern power systems due to rapid uptake of smartgrid technologies and renewables necessitates advanced methods for verification and validation of new technology solutions before field deployment. Hardware-In-the-Loop (HIL) simulation offers a high-fidelity method for test and verification of technology solutions in a close-to-real environment. This paper develops an HIL setup for test and validation of the performance of state-of-the-art, high-speed travelling wave (TW)-based protective relays. Compared to a traditional phasor-based relay, HIL testing of a TW-based relay is more challenging from modeling, numerical computation, and hardware configuration perspectives, given the high-frequency nature of TWs. This paper studies power system modeling requirements for the HIL setup for a TW relay protecting a series-compensated transmission line. The objective is to provide a guide for HIL setup development for such a test, given the type of realtime digital simulator technology that is available. The paper further presents sample HIL test results of an actual SEL-T400L relay assessing the performance of individual protective relay elements.

articleTitle: Study of Photovoltaic Array Implementation on Residential Roofs in Puerto Rico
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: The article highlights the potential of utilizing residential rooftops in Puerto Rico for installing photovoltaic systems. Due to the island's high solar potential, the study measures residential areas using Google Earth and PVWatts software to assess suitable photovoltaic systems. The results reveal rooftop areas can generate 2–3 times more energy than the users' consumption. This excess energy can be shared with the grid and other users. The next step involves quantifying the benefits of using photovoltaic arrays on rooftops to supplement Puerto Rico's grid. By inputting data into software, the feasibility of constructing a microgrid for the housing cluster is assessed. This approach could decrease the island's reliance on fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions through renewable energy adoption.

articleTitle: Method for Decoupling and Simulation of Power Distribution Networks Using a Raspberry Pi Multi-Agent System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: This paper develops a method for decoupling and simulating distribution networks using Raspberry Pis as free-communicating parallel processing agents to solve decoupled network equations. This work establishes a framework towards real-time or near real-time simulation of such networks. Real-time power network simulation has traditionally required high-cost, dedicated hardware and software. Computation with Raspberry Pis offers an economical entry point for researchers interested in real-time applications, and it advances the understanding of network decoupling for parallel computing purposes. The application to electric power distribution networks relies on a network decoupling methodology similar to the published description of the SSN method developed by OPAL-RT. Decoupling and simulation using Raspberry Pis or a multi-core PC require less processing cores compared to prior attempts on dedicated real-time hardware. The current work has been tested on the IEEE 9 bus system and provides clear proof of concept.

articleTitle: On Learning-Based Model for Dynamic Granular Prediction of Power Outages Under Extreme Events
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: As the trend of climate change continues, an increase in the severity of extreme weather events is expected, posing a significant threat to the electric power infrastructure. The efficiency of service restoration efforts can be enhanced by having access to a highly granular outage forecasting tool with long lead times. In this study, we propose to develop and implement a multi-model framework as an operational tool that utilizes a dynamic, granular, multi-day outage forecasting model based on operational weather forecasts and detailed component outage information. To address the uneven distribution of different types of weather events and make better use of the time-series data, a long-short-term-memory (LSTM)-based variational autoencoder (VAE) framework was developed to sample synthetic data and address data imbalance. With the balanced data, a prediction model was developed to estimate outages given a period of weather forecasts. The performance of the framework is demonstrated through several comparative studies.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Reliability of AC Optimal Power Flow Deep Learning Proxies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: Optimal Power Flow (OPF) is a challenging problem in power systems, and recent research has explored the use of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) to approximate OPF solutions with reduced computational times. While these approaches show promising accuracy and efficiency, there is a lack of analysis of their robustness. This paper addresses this gap by investigating the factors that lead to both successful and suboptimal predictions in DNN-based OPF solvers. It identifies power system features and DNN characteristics that contribute to higher prediction errors and offers insights on mitigating these challenges when designing deep learning models for OPF.

articleTitle: Hybrid AC/DC Static Transmission Expansion Planning Using a New Efficient Iterated Greedy Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: In recent years, High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission has become a technically and economically feasible technology, to the point that HVDC networks integrated with AC systems are being developed. However, only a few research works address Transmission Network Expansion Planning (TNEP) considering both AC and DC networks. To develop an AC/DC TNEP approach, precise models that describe the behavior of the transmission lines and their associated converter stations in DC are required. This article proposes a formulation based on a non-convex model and a heuristic optimization method to solve the AC/DC TNEP. The implementation is based on Julia using the Garver AC/DC 6-bus, the IEEE 14-bus AC/DC, and IEEE AC 24-bus test systems.

articleTitle: A Privacy-Aware Federated Learning Framework for Distributed Energy Resource Analytics in Constrained Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Latin America (ISGT-LA)
abstract: To be resilient against extreme weather events, the rural communities in Puerto Rico are leveraging distributed energy resources (DER). However, computing frameworks sup-porting the grid in critical decision-making are still largely centralized. Sensitive consumer data are transmitted over the Internet or cellular networks to a secondary or tertiary node. It guarantees better situational awareness at the cost of a wider attack surface, jeopardizing user privacy, as more DER come online. Cloud, Edge, and Fog computing all require data aggregation at some level. This paper introduces a privacy-aware federated learning framework that leverages the Fog model by pushing analytics all the way to the DER and load assets. These local models train on individual asset data and transmit only learned parameters (such as weights) over secure communications to a global decision-maker. By abstracting personally identifiable consumer data without impacting decision optimality, this framework better aligns with distributed power generation paradigm.
